name: Phi-4 Mini Instruct
definition: Phi-4 Mini Instruct is a small dense multilingual instruction model developed by Microsoft in the Phi-4 Mini family. It has 3.8B parameters, supports 128K tokens of context, accepts Text and produces Text. Its primary role is small-model reasoning, instruction following and long-context applications.

key_topics: small-model reasoning, instruction following and long-context applications

training.summary: Microsoft reports roughly 5T training tokens, 21 days on 512 A100-80G GPUs and a June 2024 cutoff for public data. Post-training focuses on instruction following, reasoning and multilingual use in a compact parameter budget.

deployments.notes: Small size makes optimized CPU/GPU/edge deployment practical.
Available through Microsoft model distribution channels.

hardware.summary: At 3.8B parameters, the model is suitable for consumer GPUs and some CPU/edge deployments after quantization. The 128K window can nevertheless consume significant KV-cache memory; small weights do not mean small long-context runtime memory.

limitations: Long-context memory can dominate despite the small weight footprint.
Language quality is not uniform across all 23 listed languages.
Small models may require retrieval/tools for broad factual coverage.
